target_name: Asset-Light Profit Scaling Behind A Moat
rationale: This is a one-leg swap on the archive's Knowledge-Backed Gross Profit Scaling that recombines two legs already present in the archive (asset-light gross-profit growth and the 3-year gross-margin MA gate), and the substituted gate is essentially the documented gross-profitability/margin level effect, so the incremental learning is narrow even though the construction and sign are internally coherent.

target_name: Gross Profit Per Employee Without Plant
rationale: Labor-productivity growth as an unbooked-human-capital proxy is a genuinely new channel for this archive and the expression matches the hypothesis and sign, though be aware the second leg alone is close to the asset-growth/investment anomaly (partly absorbed by CMA in FF5) and emp is coarsely reported.

Swapping the margin level for a five-year margin trend is a substantive, well-motivated design change that separates structurally thin-margin businesses from firms actually losing pricing power, and the expression's direction matches the stated negative sign; the main risk is that the trend leg alone captures known profitability-change/earnings-momentum effects.

Normalizing R&D by the firm's own five-year average is a genuine within-firm reframing that is distinct from the archive's level and one-year-change R&D legs and orthogonal to the published R&D-intensity anomaly, with a consistent sign; watch for unstable ratios when the historical R&D base is near zero and for the coverage loss from requiring five years of reported xrd.

This is the fifth conditional variant in an acquisition family where four different gates (no R&D, low margin, goodwill overhang, buy-vs-build) all produced nearly identical alphas with flat slopes, strongly implying the aqc leg drives everything and a new gate is cosmetic; the gate is also mechanically contaminated since acquisitions themselves inflate consolidated gross profit growth.

Advertising intensity is a well-documented published anomaly, and COALESCE(xad,0) collapses the roughly three-quarters of firms that never report advertising to an exact zero, so the ratio becomes largely a reporter/consumer-industry indicator — precisely the zero-mass defect the proposal claims to avoid.
